transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-07-15
- Time: 14:00 PT
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood), Liam O'Connor (Redwood), Priya Desai (Cinder Labs), Marcus Lee (Cinder Labs), Ana Gomez (Cinder Labs)

Summary:
Short-form podcast-style interview with Cinder Labs about their use of Redwood for inference in production. Conversational, marketing-focused: benefits, anecdotal metrics, product anecdotes, and a couple of light technical asides for listeners.

Topics:
- Why Cinder picked Redwood
- Performance & cost outcomes
- Private deployment considerations and security
- Customer stories / specific features (Dedicated capacity, smart routing)
- Next steps for episode production and approvals

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hi everyone, welcome. This is Sofia from Redwood, thanks so much for joining our little podcast today. Um, we're just gonna do, like, 25-30 minutes of chat, very informal. Liam's gonna capture audio and, uh, we'll record. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Priya: Good, thanks. Excited. Thanks for having us, Sofia. Hey Marcus, Ana.
[00:14] Marcus: Hey. Thanks for the invite.
[00:16] Ana: Morning!
[00:18] Liam: All good, audio check — one, two, three — sounds good on my end.
[00:22] Sofia: Great. So quick intro: Priya leads ML at Cinder Labs, Marcus is their CTO, Ana runs product marketing. Um, quick warm-up question: Priya, how would you describe Cinder's product and the role of LLMs in it?
[00:37] Priya: Sure. Cinder Labs builds a developer platform for edge robotics, uh, where we embed language features in developer tooling and on-device assistant flows. We've been using LLMs for code gen, operator instructions, and importantly for summarization of telemetry. The models power a lot of our user-facing flows.
[00:52] Sofia: Nice. And when did you first start production—like, when did you start serving inference?
[00:57] Priya: We moved past prototypes in early 2024, and by Q3 we had a live system. Initially we self-hosted models on GPUs but, uh, the operational overhead started to, you know, get in the way. That's when we started talking to Redwood.
[01:11] Marcus: Yeah, the infra was creeping up—costs and latency jitter. We needed more predictable throughput for our evals and real-time flows.
[01:18] Sofia: Can you describe what you measure to know if a new infra is working? Like latency, p99, cost per 1k tokens?
[01:25] Priya: Definitely latency p95/p99, tail latency for interactive sessions, and cost per inference — both server and token-level. We also look at error rates and then, more product-y metrics, like task success rate for the assistant flows. After Redwood, we saw a 35% lower cost per useful response and p99 down from 1.2s to 450ms for typical agent flows.
[01:45] Ana: I'll add, from a marketing perspective, the improved responsiveness made demos way smoother and conversion from trial to paid went up.
[01:53] Sofia: Love that. Did you use Redwood Hosted first, or did you go straight to Dedicated or Private?
[01:58] Priya: We started with Hosted to iterate quickly, then moved to Redwood Dedicated pools for predictable throughput. More recently, for compliance reasons, we evaluated Private - the VPC option - and ended up with a hybrid: core user flows on Dedicated, sensitive data on Private.
[02:14] Marcus: The hybrid routing was actually—uh—super helpful. We route by tenant policy, so regulated customers hit the Private VPC path. It kept things simple for us.
[02:23] Sofia: There are always questions about security — SOC2, KMS, SSO. How did that process go?
[02:28] Priya: We ran a security review; Redwood's SOC 2 attestation and KMS integrations were helpful. There were a few questions about audit log retention and data residency — Liam? the logs?
[02:39] Marcus: Right, we needed 7 years of audit logs for one customer (laughs). Redwood provided guidance on retention and the private control plane made the auditors happy.
[02:46] Sofia: Nice. On the technical side, any surprised wins or pain points?
[02:50] Priya: We were surprised how much batching + KV cache reuse improved throughput for our streaming calls. The compiler/kernels optimizations Redwood mentioned actually translated to real cost savings for us. One small pain point: initial model variance between dev and prod — we had to pin versions to avoid drift.
[03:06] Marcus: Also, the model catalog helped. We tried a quantized variant of a base model to cut cost; it was a small quality delta but a big performance win.
[03:14] Sofia: Good to hear. For the audience — quick elevator pitch, why Redwood?
[03:18] Priya: Predictable performance and fewer Ops headaches. We wanted our engineers focusing on product, not infra. Redwood's routing and rollout features let us do canary deploys with confidence.
[03:26] Ana: From a customer perspective, the reliability was key — we could promise SLAs because the infra was stable.
[03:31] Sofia: Okay turning to a couple fun prompts for the podcast — any memorable customer story where inference made a difference?
[03:36] Marcus: Yeah — we had a customer whose field technicians used our voice assistant in low-connectivity environments; being able to serve the model with low tail latency meant a truck roll was avoided and they called it a multi-million-dollar win.
[03:47] Priya: That story actually led to our Sales team prioritizing edge features.
[03:51] Sofia: Classic. Quick tangent: did you ever run into vendor lock-in worries?
[03:55] Priya: We evaluated that. The platform approach helped — Redwood supports multiple model variants and export paths. We maintain a small compatibility shim so we can run a model locally if needed.
[04:06] Sofia: Awesome. We'll do a few listener Qs — no, actually just two rapid-fire ones: one, what's one tip for teams starting out? two, what's next for Cinder?
[04:15] Priya: Tip: invest in good telemetry and proms for inference — measure success end-to-end. Next: expanding multimodal support and tighter offline sync for edge devices.
[04:25] Marcus: And keep models versioned and have a rollback plan.
[04:28] Ana: Marketing note — expect a short case study from us on the website next month.
[04:33] Sofia: Lovely. Okay, closing logistics — we'll send an audio draft and a short written summary. Can you confirm the approvals? Priya will sign the speaker release, Marcus will OK technical quotes, Ana will provide logo and headshots.
[04:45] Priya: Yep, I'll sign by the end of next week.
[04:47] Marcus: I'll review the technical quotes.
[04:49] Ana: I'll send assets to Liam.
[04:51] Liam: I'll compile the edit and share timeline.
[04:54] Sofia: Perfect. Any last things to call out?
[04:57] Priya: If you need short soundbites about cost savings, use the 35% number and the tail latency metric — those resonated in our GTM.
[05:06] Sofia: Great. Ok we'll wrap. Thanks so much, everyone, for being candid and for the great stories — this will be a fun episode.
[05:14] Marcus: Thanks, Sofia.
[05:15] Ana: Thanks!
[05:16] Priya: Thanks.
